title: Client prefetch safety islands - PRD scratchpad
body:
Overview:
This is a working PRD sketch for a small-surface feature we are calling "client prefetch safety islands". The goal: enable SDKs and client apps to prefetch partial streaming outputs and candidate tool results speculatively while guaranteeing that any speculative tool invocation or sensitive data is isolated until explicitly committed by the server-side policy.

Why this?
- Customers want lower perceived latency for interactive experiences (mobile chat, code assistant, search UI) without increasing risk of accidental tool invocation, double-billing, or leaking user PII to tool integrations.
- Current incremental/streaming designs blur the line between a candidate suggestion and a committed action. SDKs often need ergonomic primitives to express "speculate but don't call tools yet".

Problem statement (concrete):
1) Client-side prefetching often triggers tool-call side effects when naive SDKs rehydrate or replay a session (e.g., during reconnect or when a developer auto-runs suggested actions).
2) Partial/typed structured outputs streamed by the Hosted API can contain fields that map to connectors (email.send, calendar.create). Without clear separation, devs accidentally create side effects.
3) Customers want to preview low-latency results on mobile while preserving an explicit commit step that floats through the platform (for billing, audit, and safety checks).

Design principles:
- Safety islands: speculative artifacts (text deltas, parsed actions, candidate tool payloads) must be clearly labeled and cryptographically separated from "commit tokens" that enable server-side execution.
- Minimal API surface: add a tiny expressible contract that SDKs can adopt (prefetch=true, speculative-id=UUID, commit-token absent).
- No silent escalation: server will not run tool calls for any speculative-id unless a commit-token is presented and validated (policy checks performed).
- Observability and billing: speculative tokens tracked but not billed as executed; commit events generate normal billing and auditable logs.

Proposed runtime behavior (sketch):
- Client opens streaming call: POST /v1/streams with header X-Redwood-Prefetch: speculative and body {
    session_id: S, spec_id: u1, prefetch: true, model: rwd-3-sm
